transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-22
Time: 08:00 PT / 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Daniel Cho (Redwood CSM), Lena Ortiz (Head of ML, OrbitAI), Marcus Young (Infra Lead), Sofia Park (CTO), Evan Liu (Product)
Links shared: 1) preliminary cost model spreadsheet (drive.link/benchmark-orbitai), 2) Redwood Dedicated brochure (redwood.link/dedicated), 3) benchmark runner repo (git.link/redwood-bench-runner)

Summary (auto gen, may be partial):
- POC focus: validate per-token unit economics for OrbitAI NLU pipelines, confirm batching and caching knobs, run latency/cost benchmarks across hosted and dedicated modes.
- Success criteria agreed: end-to-end 95th p99 latency < 350ms for short chat use-case, average token cost <= $0.0009 (target), KW accuracy regressions < 1% on curated eval set, and a defined ramp timeline (pilot 2 weeks, scale check 6 weeks).
- Next steps: share cost model, run benchmarks, collect traces, schedule dedicated capacity demo.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Morgan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me okay?
[00:03] Lena Ortiz: yeah loud and clear, thanks Alex.
[00:07] Alex Morgan: cool, i'll do a quick context, Redwood — we focus on inference serving and cost/perf tradeoffs, today want to scope POC: success criteria, workload sizing, bench plan and timelines. Priya, wanna intro?
[00:18] Priya Shah: yeah hi all, priya se on infra and perf, i'll be running the bench and tuning batching/caching, happy to dig into their trace and suggest quantization/strategy.
[00:26] Marcus Young: thanks. quick note - we're evaluating both hosted and a dedicated reserved pool, budget is... constrained; would like a predictable per-token estimate we can present to execs.
[00:36] Alex Morgan: totally. can you give a 30k foot on the workload? qps, prompt lengths, top models?
[00:42] Lena Ortiz: sure. this is primarily our customer-facing NLU assistant, average request is ~18 tokens input + 40 tokens generated, tail up to 200 tokens. baseline qps is 35 sustained, spikes to 200 qps for short windows. model is currently a 13B open LLM, we're open to smaller / quantized variants for cost.
[01:03] Evan Liu: and critical is p99 latency under 500ms for chat, if we hit 350-400 that's even better. cost target is about $0.001 per token end-to-end but we want see if Redwood can get it lower with batching/cache.
[01:18] Priya Shah: ok that helps. couple knobs we'll examine: batching window/size, prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts, sequence-length aware kernel selection, and int8/4 quantization options. also routing to cheaper model variants on non-critical paths.
[01:33] Daniel Cho: also want to flag security requirements — SSO (SAML), SOC2 compliance, encrypted logs with KMS — is that captured?
[01:41] Alex Morgan: yes we'll include security pack, Redwood Private has KMS/HSM options and audit logs, note the doc link.

[01:50] Marcus Young: on cost math — how do you usually estimate per-token? we've seen vendor quotes vary a lot and the main unknown is the effective tokens/sec when batching and cache hits.
[01:58] Priya Shah: good question. we break it down into: model compute cost per token (GPU runtime), orchestration overhead, and then amortize fixed costs (reserved capacity) across expected qps. effective per-token = raw token compute * (1 - cache_hit_rate) / batching_efficiency + overhead. so if you hit 60% cache for prefixes and batch sizes average 8, your per-token op cost drops significantly.
[02:25] Lena Ortiz: got it, can you show numbers for our workload?
[02:28] Priya Shah: rough back-of-envelope: for a 13B fp16 model on A100 style hardware, raw compute might be ~0.0006 token, with batching and cache we can get to ~0.00035. with infra overhead + networking + small margins maybe end-to-end ~0.0009-0.0012 on hosted. on dedicated reserved we can squeeze lower depending on utilization - maybe down to ~0.0006. these are preliminary.
[02:52] Alex Morgan: just to be clear, those numbers depend heavily on prompt reuse and skew, if you have many unique prompts caching is less effective.
[02:59] Marcus Young: our prompts have a lot of repetition for the initial system prompt and some user intents, i'd estimate 40-50% prefix reuse.
[03:07] Priya Shah: perfect, at 45% reuse our model would look more like 0.00055-0.00075/token hosted. batching also reduces per-token if latency SLO allows a slightly larger micro-batching window.
[03:18] Evan Liu: what about KV cache invalidation? we rotate user contexts frequently.
[03:22] Priya Shah: eviction strategy important — session length and user stickiness drive hit rate. we can configure per-route cache TTLs; for ephemeral ctxs you get less benefit. we can also do smart prefix canonicalization to increase hits.
[03:34] Sofia Park: curious about the bench — how long does a typical benchmark run and what do you need from us?
[03:39] Priya Shah: we'll run representative load against either our hosted endpoint or a temporary dedicated pool. typical bench window is 30-60 minutes per config to capture steady-state and spike behavior. we need: a) request traces (two weeks ideal) including token counts and timestamps b) sample prompts c) target SLOs. we'll provide a runner script and config.
[03:59] Alex Morgan: and we'll capture p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, cache hit rates, and cost projection per 1M tokens.
[04:09] Lena Ortiz: can you do multiple model variants in the same bench? like 13B fp16 vs 13B int8 quant vs 7B?
[04:15] Priya Shah: yes we recommend testing 3 variants: current 13B fp16 baseline, 13B quant (int8/4) and a 7B optimized variant. we can also simulate routing policies where non-critical requests go to cheaper variants.
[04:27] Marcus Young: how do you treat burst windows in cost modeling? we have periodic spikes that last 5-10 minutes.
[04:33] Alex Morgan: great point — costing has two components: steady-state amortized unit cost and burst provisioning. for burst we model either autoscale (higher spot-like pricing) or reserved + burst capacity. reserved capacity reduces unit cost but risks underutilization. we'll run scenarios in the spreadsheet.
[04:48] Evan Liu: will you include tail latency impact when batching? sometimes batching increases p99.
[04:52] Priya Shah: yes, batching tradeoff explicit in the model: we show expected average cost vs p99 as a function of batching window and max batch size. in practice we apply latency-aware batching where high-priority requests bypass batch or use smaller window.
[05:06] Lena Ortiz: i want to see a concrete success criteria list for the POC. can we draft that now?
[05:10] Alex Morgan: sure. draft: 1) p99 latency for chat flow <= 350ms under 100 qps sustained; 2) average token cost <= $0.0009 on hosted benchmark with 45% cache hit; 3) model accuracy regressions <1% on eval set; 4) secure connection with SAML + KMS encryption and audit logs enabled. agree?
[05:29] Lena Ortiz: yes that's fine but add item about scalability check for spikes to 200 qps for 10 minutes.
[05:35] Alex Morgan: added. any objections?
[05:37] Sofia Park: fine from infra side. Marcus can confirm resource constraints.
[05:40] Marcus Young: sounds good. also include billing cadence and reporting, exec summary for finance.
[05:45] Daniel Cho: we'll provide a one-pager cost summary that's CFO friendly.
[05:48] 
[05:50] Alex Morgan: timeline proposal: we provision bench infra and run first set within 7 business days once we get traces. pilot phase two weeks to validate. then a scale check in 6 weeks. so rough calendar: traces by 12/26, bench run week of 12/28, initial report by 01/02, pilot 01/05 - 01/19, scale check mid-February.
[06:12] Marcus Young: aggressive but okay. question around data retention and logs, we need log retention TTL, does Redwood store request logs in hosted?
[06:20] Alex Morgan: hosted stores minimal request metadata by default; full transcript/log retention configurable. we'll share retention options and SOC2 controls. for Private deployment logs can remain in your VPC.
[06:33] Evan Liu: any gotchas with quantization on accuracy? we've seen odd hallucination increases with int4 on some prompts.
[06:38] Priya Shah: yes quantization can affect LLM quality; part of the bench is eval sets and A/B compare. we also recommend targeted quantization only for non-critical paths. we'll measure perplexity and downstream task F1.
[06:52] Lena Ortiz: ok. one more on pricing: is there a minimum committed spend for dedicated?
[06:56] Alex Morgan: yes Dedicated has reserved commit tiers; we'll include example price bands in the sheet. smaller pilots can use hosted with burst capacity.
[07:04] Marcus Young: can Redwood export per-token billing breakdown so our finance folks can map to internal cost centers?
[07:08] Daniel Cho: yes we provide token-level cost breakdowns and per-route tags for allocation.
[07:13] Priya Shah: for the bench, we'll send the runner and ask you to run one session to ensure network/firewall is ok, if not we'll run from our side with a temporary sandbox.
[07:24] Alex Morgan: ok let's recap action items...
[07:26] Lena Ortiz: sorry one quick question — do you support KMS key rotation policies if we do Private?
[07:30] Alex Morgan: yes KMS rotation supported, we can map to your HSM as well.
[07:34] Alex Morgan: recap: Marcus to share traces and sample prompts by 2026-12-26, Alex to send cost model and pricing by 2026-12-24, Priya to provide bench runner + script by 2026-12-27, Sofia to confirm SSO/NDA by 2026-12-28. Redwood will run first bench the week of 12/28 and deliver report first week of Jan.
[07:58] Evan Liu: ok thanks all, looking forward.
[08:00] Alex Morgan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with links.

End of transcript.
